newsitem.title: USA: U.S. JUNE WHOLESALE INVENTORIES ROSE 1.9 PCT.
newsitem.headline: U.S. JUNE WHOLESALE INVENTORIES ROSE 1.9 PCT.

text.p: Commerce Department report of wholesale inventories and sales, seasonally adjusted.
(Billions of dollars) Jun May--Rev from Jun96
(Billions of dollars) Jun May--Rev from Jun96
The 1.9 percent jump in June inventories was the largest monthly increase since April 1982, when they climbed by 2.0 percent, the department said.

The June stock-to-sales ratio for merchant wholesalers, seasonally adjusted, was 1.25 months' worth, up from 1.23 months' worth in May. The department said it was the highest level for the ratio since October last year when it also was at 1.25 months' worth.
The ratio is a measure of how many months it would take to sell existing inventories at the current sales pace.
One of the biggest increases in inventories was for new cars and parts, which increased 5.1 percent from May to a value of $28.25 billion in June. Auto inventories had risen only 1.7 percent in May.
Stocks of professional and commercial equipment and supplies grew by 3.1 percent in June to $23.54 billion after a much smaller 0.6 percent May decrease.
